fields.label: Pattern (phrase)
fields.description: A substring match against the field(s) below, lowercase, e.g. 'gosi' or 'current account to mr. medhat'. Regex is not supported in v1 — per the build spec, deterministic phrase rules come before probabilistic scoring, and a plain substring is the simplest thing that's still fully explainable to the accountant reviewing a suggestion.

fields.options:
Remarks
Against Account
Remarks + Against Account
fields.label: Match Field
fields.description: Which transaction field(s) this pattern is checked against. Against Account alone is rarely safe on its own — the historical data shows the same counterparty appearing under several different categories — prefer Remarks or the combined option unless the evidence below says otherwise.

fields.label: Target Line
fields.description: The Cash Flow Forecast line (the 'G' / New Class category) this rule suggests when it matches. Never a freeform label — always one of the approved, already-configured lines, so a rule can never invent a category.

fields.options:
Candidate
Under Review
Approved
Active
Suspended
Retired
fields.label: Status
fields.description: Candidate: mined automatically, nobody has looked at it yet. Under Review: a reviewer has it open. Approved: a human signed off, not yet live. Active: actually used to suggest classifications. Suspended: temporarily pulled (e.g. rolling precision dropped) without deleting its history. Retired: permanently done. Only Active rules are ever used in classify_transaction — mining, approving, and using are three separate, deliberate steps, never one.

fields.label: Historical Support
fields.description: How many already-classified historical transactions this pattern matched, at mining time.

fields.label: Historical Precision
fields.description: Of those matches, the share that were actually classified as Target Line. A rule mined with anything less than very high precision should not reach Active without a reviewer understanding why.

fields.label: Sample Transactions
fields.description: A handful of real historical remarks this pattern matched, shown to the reviewer as concrete evidence rather than an abstract precision number.

fields.label: Rolling Precision
fields.description: confirmed / (confirmed + corrected), updated on every accountant decision — the live version of Historical Precision, from real usage rather than the mining snapshot. A rule whose rolling precision drops below its approval threshold should be flagged for review, never silently rewritten.

fields.label: Superseded By
fields.description: If a reviewer replaces this rule with a refined version rather than editing it in place — keeps the old rule's history intact for audit instead of overwriting it.
